{{short description|American researcher into cannabinoids}}
'''Alexandros Makriyannis''' (born September 9, 1939) is an American biochemist and professor of chemistry and chemical biology in the department of medicinal chemistry at [[Northeastern University]] in [[Boston, Massachusetts]], where he directs the Center for Drug Discovery and holds the George Behrakis Chair of Pharmaceutical Biotechnology.<ref name=northeastern>{{cite web |title=Alexandros Makriyannis |url=https://cos.northeastern.edu/faculty/alexandros-makriyannis/ |publisher=Northeastern University College of Science |accessdate=2 December 2018}}</ref> His research has focused on the biochemical basis of the [[endocannabinoid system]] and on the development of synthetic [[cannabinoid]]s.

==Scientific career==
Makriyannis studied chemistry at the [[University of Cairo]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Pioneer in Chemical Biology |url=https://www.ellines.com/en/famous-greeks/30216-pioneer-in-chemical-biology/ |accessdate=3 January 2019 |work=Ellines}}</ref> He then earned his Ph.D. in medicinal chemistry at the [[University of Kansas]] and went on to research synthetic organic chemistry at the [[University of California, Berkeley]]. He worked at [[Smith, Kline & French]] Laboratories and [[Tufts Medical School]] and then at the [[University of Connecticut]], where he was later appointed Distinguished Professor of Medicinal Chemistry and Professor of Molecular and Cell Biology and Pharmacology.<ref name=addforum>{{cite web |title=Alexandros Makriyannis |url=http://www.advancingdrugdevelopment.com/2018/08/06/alexandros-makriyannis/ |publisher=Advancing Drug Development Forum |accessdate=2 December 2018 |date=2018-08-06 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190103082958/http://www.advancingdrugdevelopment.com/2018/08/06/alexandros-makriyannis/ |archive-date=3 January 2019 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref name="acsmed" /> He moved to Northeastern University in 2005.<ref name="acsmed">{{cite web |title=Alexandros Makriyannis, Ph.D. |url=https://www.acsmedchem.org/?nd=Makriyannis |publisher=American Chemical Society, Division of Medicinal Chemistry |accessdate=2 December 2018}}</ref>

Makriyannis is director of the Center for Drug Discovery at Northeastern University, which he founded in 2005.<ref name=addforum /> His work has identified the structure of cannabinoid receptors in the brain, helping to elucidate the psychoactive properties of some of these substances<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nih.gov/news-events/nih-research-matters/cannabinoid-receptor-structure-revealed|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170106073842/https://www.nih.gov/news-events/nih-research-matters/cannabinoid-receptor-structure-revealed|url-status=dead|archive-date=January 6, 2017|title=Cannabinoid receptor structure revealed|date=November 1, 2016|publisher=National Institutes of Health (NIH)}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://news.northeastern.edu/2016/10/20/structure-of-the-brains-marijuana-receptor-revealed/|title=Structure of the brain's 'marijuana receptor' revealed|last1=Singer|first1=Thea|date=October 20, 2016|website=News@Northeastern|publisher=Northeastern University}}</ref> and to point towards modifications in the receptors so as to retain the positive effects of cannabinoids while eliminating the negative ones.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.gqmagazine.fr/pop-culture/sorties/articles/peut-on-fumer-de-lherbe-sans-etre-stone-/57087|title=Peut-on fumer de l'herbe sans être stone ?|last1=Perrier|first1=Jean|date=October 19, 2017|work=GQ France|language=fr-FR|trans-title=Could we smoke weed without getting stoned?}}</ref> These studies have informed the development by Makriyannis and his collaborators of synthetic compounds with a view to their use as [[cannabinergic]] probes or as medications in [[drug addiction]]<ref>{{cite web|url=https://news.northeastern.edu/2018/08/03/can-the-opioid-crisis-be-fixed/|title=Can the opioid crisis be fixed?|last1=Davi|first1=Christine Regan|date=August 3, 2018|website=News@Northeastern|publisher=Northeastern University}}</ref> and in [[obesity]] and [[metabolic disorder]]s.<ref name="acsmed" /> A more recent research interest has been the study of drug interactions with [[protein targeting|protein targets]] in membranes.<ref name="acsmed" /> His research has been reported in over 470 publications and his group has filed more than 40 patents.<ref name=addforum />

==Biotechnology Startups==
Makriyannis has founded two biotechnology startups in [[Burlington, Massachusetts|Burlington]], MA dedicated to bringing new and innovative drugs to the market place for human diseases that can be modulated by the endocannabinoid system:

* MAKScientific (2004)  
* PafosPharma (2017)
